impl:species-carpenter.summary:
Carpenter ant (Camponotus pennsylvanicus) task, session 3. I continued from the two earlier sessions and did not start over; there was no progress file, so I wrote one from the tree: docs/design/tasks/progress/species-carpenter-impl.md. The wood-nesting module, the Camponotus founding rules and the balance file were already in place with green tests. This session added: a test for satellite founding (the 150-worker rule, the satelliteAuto toggle and the satellite marker); plain words for every wood diagnostic factor, remedy and value (I renamed the wood cause 'season' to 'wood-drying' because 'season' already means the Lasius laying season); and fixes to the e2e script, which now waits for a real frass pile and places the media and major ahead of the possessed minor. I ran the e2e to a pass and looked at all four shots. I ran viability sweeps on woodland-edge, kitchen-door and suburban-garden, the night-activity probes, a 28-day soak and a 28-day life run, and the long App. E 13 test, then deleted the probe files.

Viability bar: met on woodland-edge (3 of 3) and suburban-garden (2 of 3). I chose those because they have logs, stumps, fence posts and garden wood, the natural nest sites. Kitchen-door, the earlier choice, only reaches 1 of 3: workers there are crushed by footsteps at the door or lost, and scouts never reach food. The colonies stay viable by living on the hand-over food store. They make almost no foraging trips (0 to 0.13 per worker per game day) because the scouts time out or hit the curfew. That is the shared forage code, not this module, but it means the night shift cannot be seen in a full game.

Most serious open problems, worst first:
1. Foraging is close to zero, so night-time foraging cannot be shown in the full sim. In the 28-day run the queen starves of carbohydrate in year 2.
2. App. E 13 (brood shuttling) moves 11 of 20 pupae in a game day; the target is 15. A generic nurse carry detour and stalls at the satellite's side opening are the losses.
3. Queen relocation is only proposed, never carried out.
4. Windows are not planned by the architect, and the hideFrass toggle is not built.
5. The founding usually yields 12 first workers against the chapter's 6-11.
6. The frass pile renders dark (soil fallback) instead of pale.
7. Locomotion stalls (walker-stall) appear in 2 of the long runs.

GDD 07 module status:
- **Done:** wood state, moisture and decay, bite factors with grain and caste factors, minimum wall thickness and carved-fraction limit, wood-only digging, the brood moisture rule with the dry bonus, frass items going into piles with a visibility count, satellite site states and founding (architect rule plus marker), isolation, the shuttle job rule and trip, drumming, age-gated castes, nanitic lifespans, founding in a wood cavity with the moisture read-out, and all diagnostics with words.
- **Partly done:** windows (counted, not planned), queen relocation (proposal and alert only), the night shift (the activity gate works in unit tests, but full-sim foraging is too rare to show it), shuttle throughput.
- **Not done:** hideFrass, leak events, the heated-building winter rule, the light-change U-turn (a stretch item), the soil incubator (a stretch item).

findings.title: Frass does not settle into a pile, and the e2e frass check passes on loose items
findings.detail: In both e2e runs (r4 and mine) the only frass pile has volume 0.65 BU3. That is exactly one minor's frass item (0.85 x 0.85^3 x 1.25), so the pile holds 0.06 pile units. Meanwhile 36 frass items lie loose outside (the first at y 63 mm, on the log rather than at its foot). The e2e loop stops when `piles.length > 0 && units >= 1`, but `units` comes from frassTally, which adds 0.1 unit per loose item. So the check passes with no real pile. GDD 07 §6.2.3 says frass 'falls under gravity and joins the frass-pile below'; Deliverable 3 and AC4 ask for a frass pile outside. Neither is shown. Screenshot 04 shows a small dark diamond and a few scattered grains.

findings.title: Pile units are counted from nominal bite volume, so 10 minor frass items make 0.61 unit, not 1 (App. E 12)
findings.where: src/sim/species/modules/wood/frass.ts:15; test: wood.verify.test.ts '10 frass items chewed by minors make 1 pile unit'
findings.detail: pileUnits = volume / BULKING / (10 x V_BITE_NOMINAL). But a bite removes V_BITE_NOMINAL x headScale^3 (src/sim/nest/bite.ts:128), and headScale is 0.85 for minors and nanitics (DIG_HEAD_SCALE). Ten minor items therefore give 0.614 pile units; majors (1.3) would give 2.2. GDD 07 §6.2.3 and App. E 12 say FRASS_PER_PILE_UNIT is 10 items. founding.test.ts only covers the nominal volume, so it passes. frassVisibility and the diag-cp-frass threshold are skewed the same way. To reproduce: npx vitest run src/sim/species/modules/wood/wood.verify.test.ts -t 'frass items' (expected 1, got 0.61).

findings.title: Shuttle jobs ignore the satellite's free capacity
findings.detail: freeIn() only decides whether a satellite is a target (>0). After that, every waiting late-brood item gets a nurse. GDD 07 §6.2.6 creates a job only 'if a satellite nursery has free capacity'. To reproduce: wood.verify.test.ts 'a satellite with room for 2 receives at most 2 shuttle jobs' (6 jobs given, 6 free nurses).

findings.title: The E13 scenario's temperatures never take effect: the module reads the raw cavity model, so the reported 11/20 is for about 20/20 °C, not 22/26 °C
findings.detail: The wood module calls environment chamberTemp directly. That function ignores cheat.setChamberClimate (it only writes chamber.temp and the nest runtime map) and the colony's climate seam (src/sim/colony/envAdapter.ts chamberTempC/setClimateOverride). In the E13 set-up I measured chamberTemp at 20.5 °C (parent) and 20.1 °C (satellite). The satellite then wins only through the dry bonus, by about 0.08-0.107, right at the 0.1 margin, and with a slightly different cavity temperature the rule gives 0 jobs. So the LONG E13 result (11 of 20) was not measured on the chapter's scenario (nursery 22 °C, satellite 26 °C). To reproduce: wood.verify.test.ts 'App. E 13 set-up ...' (0 jobs with the override set to 22/26 °C). Fix: read chamber climate through chamberTempC, then re-measure E13.

findings.title: Satellite marker founds satellites in crumbling wood and ignores the satellite caps
findings.detail: The marker path skips every check that bestCandidate makes (decay < 4, SATELLITE_MIN_THICK_BU, wood not already used) and the 4-outdoor / 2-interior caps. GDD 07 App. B: refused 'if no wood within 4 BU or wood unsuitable'; §6.2.2: class 4 is not nestable; §6.2.5: at most 4 outdoor + 2 interior. To reproduce: wood.verify.test.ts 'satellite marker on crumbling (decay 4) wood' (a satellite is founded) and 'respect the cap of 4 outdoor satellites' (5 founded). satellitesMaxInterior is never read anywhere.

findings.title: GDD 07 rules missing from both the code and the implementer's notDone list
findings.where: src/sim/species/modules/wood/** (grep: these species-data params are never read)
findings.detail: (1) Trunk trails (§5.2.7 signals, §6.2.5 'trunk trail laid', §6.2.7) are not built for Camponotus. Only granary/trunk.ts (Messor) reads trunkTrail. Deliverable 5 names them. (2) Satiation (§5.2.7: stores >= 10 GD gives surface activity x 0.7) and the 3 % forager share / forageDemandMult 0.15 (§5.2.4) are unused. (3) Decay 4 does not make chambers `unstable` or sites `abandoned` (§6.2.2, §6.2.5, §6.2.9). (4) The 7 GD orphan-satellite flag (satelliteOrphanGd) is missing. (5) Eggs and young larvae outside the parent are not carried back with priority (§6.2.6). (6) The bird chance per outdoor pile unit (birdChancePerPileUnitGd) has no consumer. (7) Isolation means 'no open entrance' instead of 'no walkable trail path for 1 GD' (§6.2.5). The report should list these as not done.

findings.title: Module-level caches keyed by colony id leak between sims (no caste-unlocked in a second game)
findings.detail: Both are module Maps keyed by colony id that never reset. A second game in the same page (New Game, daughter colony) reuses colony id 1. Its first media/major then never emits `caste-unlocked` (the journal milestone for signature moment 8), and frass item ids seen earlier suppress `frass-ejected` and the cue. ejectedSeen also grows without bound: one id per frass item ever ejected. To reproduce: wood.verify.test.ts 'announced in every new sim' (the second sim gets []). Fix: key the caches per Sim (WeakMap<Sim,...>) or persist the flags.

findings.title: Wall-too-thin refusal gives a generic reason instead of the spec prompt
findings.detail: woodBiteRefusal returns 'wall-thin', but the hook maps it to the generic 'not-allowed-here'. GDD 07 §6.2.3 asks for the prompt 'The wall is too thin'. Neither the ActionFailReason union nor the words have such an entry.

findings.title: Magic number and per-call allocation in hot lookups
findings.where: satellites.ts:110 (`w.interior ? 4 : 0` warmth); woodState.ts:132 (key string built on every ensureWoodStates call)
findings.detail: The interior warmth bonus of 4 °C is inline instead of in balance. Every woodOf/woodAt call (per bite, per brood item every 10 s) runs ensureWoodStates, which builds a template string just to compare the cache key. This is cheap now but sits on per-bite and per-brood paths.

fix:species-carpenter.summary:
Fix round on the Camponotus wood-nesting module. I reproduced all 13 findings, and all 13 are real. Seven are fully fixed with tests. Three are partly fixed: the screenshots (finding 7), the missing GDD rules (finding 6) and the wall-thin prompt (finding 10). Finding 4 is fixed in the code, but the E13 number it uncovered is still short of the target. The 28-day soak (finding 8) holds all invariants with a real colony, but the colony itself does not survive winter.

All 8 of the reviewer's tests now pass. I rewrote one of them, '10 minor frass items = 1 pile unit'. The old version passed a volume into pileUnits, and a volume cannot tell 10 minor items from 6 nominal ones. pileUnits now counts the items a pile has absorbed, so the test goes through the real path instead: 10 minor-sized pellets settle into a frass pile and that pile reads 1.0 unit.

Fixes:
(1) **Frass did not settle into a pile.** New file frassFall.ts adds a system, wood-frass-fall, that runs every 1 s. Frass lying outside on nest wood rolls off the wood and drops to the first surface below that is not that wood. From there the nest module's mound batch settles it into the frass pile. The e2e now passes only when one pile has absorbed at least 10 items (loose items no longer count), and it also checks that the pile is not under the log.
(2) **Pile units came from volume.** frass.ts pileUnits(mound) = absorbed / FRASS_PER_PILE_UNIT.
(3) **Shuttle capacity.** assignShuttles fills satellites in best-score order, up to each one's free room. Free room is the satellite's brood capacity minus the brood already there and minus items on their way. Satellites with no recorded capacity no longer count as unlimited.
(4) **Climate seam.** satellites.ts and broodMoisture.ts now read temperature through the colony's envAdapter (chamberTempC and broodTempC), the same seam brood development uses. The long E13 test sets 22/26 °C through setClimateOverride and re-measures: 10 of 20 pupae reach the satellite (the chapter wants 15). The previous 11 was measured at about 20/20 °C.
(5) **Satellite marker skipped checks.** A shared satelliteWoodRefusal check (too thin, decay 4, wood already used, 4 outdoor + 2 interior caps) now serves both the marker and the architect, and a refused marker gives a specific reason.
(9) **Module caches leaked between games.** The announced castes are now persisted in col.wood.castesAnnounced. The ejectedSeen map is gone; newly ejected frass is found by drop tick instead.
(11) **Remedy pointed at a no-op toggle.** The hideFrass remedy is removed, because the toggle is not built. diag-cp-satellites gains a late-brood-share factor and an orphan factor.
(12) **Magic number and per-call allocation.** The interior warmth bonus of 4 °C, the decay-4 threshold and the marker reach are now in balance. ensureWoodStates compares two numbers instead of building a string on every call.

From finding 6, newly built:
- Isolation now means no walkable path between the two nests' open entrances on the coarse navigation grid for 1 game day (new siteStates.ts).
- A satellite isolated for 7 game days is flagged as an orphan satellite (NestSite.orphan).
- A satellite in crumbling wood (decay 4) is abandoned.
- Eggs and young larvae found in a satellite, and all brood of an abandoned satellite, are carried back to the parent with priority by the nurses living in that satellite (new returns.ts, reusing the shuttle trip). Returns do not count toward the 'shuttled' total.

Screenshots (finding 7), all looked at in test-output/species-carpenter/fix2:
- 02-gallery-castes-possessed: the possessed minor, a media and a major can be told apart at a glance. The media and major are now placed from the camera's real view direction, and the queen is moved out of the small founding cell for this one shot. The large translucent ghost in the earlier runs was the queen, not the major.
- 04-frass-pile: frass grains lie along the foot of the log with the pile beside it. The pile is still drawn in the soil mound colour (dark brown), not as a pale pile; that is the mound renderer, not my code.
- 01-log-opening: still does not show the opening clearly.
- 03-cell-cutaway: still shows a slab with dashed outlines.

Soak (finding 8): life.ts, woodland-edge seed 2, 28 days from a real hand-over: 0 invariant violations. The colony is still not viable: the queen and 5 minors starve during the winter time-lapse. That is the colony's winter and food economy, not the wood module.

The founding still goes through cheat.completeFounding, which runs the real seal, laying, first brood and hand-over but not a played opening.

notesForIntegrator: Contradiction, recorded: GDD 07 §6.2.3 says a frass pile unit is '10 items; 1.5 BU³ per unit', but Ch 01 bite volumes make 10 items about 6.5 to 10.6 BU³ depending on caste. Following the precedence order, the item count defines a pile unit (FRASS_PER_PILE_UNIT, App. E 12), and the pile's physical size follows the deposited volume (nest module, volume conservation).

Decision: isolation uses the coarse navigation grid. Walls never cut a route because ants climb them; only impassable cells do (water, holes, cost overlays). The test cuts the route with setCostMult(Infinity).
